name: Yttrium titanate
equilibrium_context: Ferromagnetic Mott insulator with a suppressed Curie point at 27 K and a reduced saturation moment

driven_states.emergent_property: Mode-selective excitation of an oxygen rotation mode at 9 THz leads at low temperatures to complete magnetic saturation and produces transient ferromagnetism up to above 80 K, that is about three times the thermodynamic transition temperature.

drive.driven_mode: oxygen rotation and tilt mode at 9 THz; the anharmonically generated distortion modulates orbital order and exchange

driven_states.source: Disa, Curtis, Fechner et al., Nature 617, 73 (2023), doi:10.1038/s41586-023-05853-8
driven_states.caveat: Above the Curie temperature this is a driven magnetization in a regime of strong ferromagnetic fluctuations, and not demonstrably long-range order. The evidence is magneto-optical. In equilibrium the material is already a ferromagnet - so the transition temperature is shifted, no new type of order is created.

threshold.quantity: nonlinear fluence dependence, saturation above a critical amplitude

gaps: Field strength not verified, fluence only as a range.
